narrative:
The model determined that you have a 99.2% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because the law school uses this prediction to decide admissions, your application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors from your academic record. Your class ranking at the end of your third year was the strongest influence, pushing the prediction strongly toward failure. Your first-year ranking was the second most important factor and also pulled the outcome toward failure. Your family income bracket ranked third and added further weight in the same direction.

Compared with students who were accepted, you finished both your first and third years in a much lower decile (2 versus an average around 6). These consistently lower academic standings relative to your classmates signaled to the model a higher risk of struggling with the bar exam. Your family’s upper-middle income level, while common among accepted students, also contributed slightly to the negative outlook in this specific case.

To improve your chances, focus on strengthening your academic performance if you retake any courses, consider targeted bar exam preparation programs, and explore schools that place less weight on these early indicators. Rebuilding a stronger record in law school coursework could significantly change future predictions. (218 words)
